title: Welcome home
caption:
Welcome to Leaf People. 🌿

Forget the inbox, the traffic, the noise. For the next sixty seconds you're somewhere else — a Colombian cloud forest, ankle-deep in leaf litter, the air thick and green.

This is an app, and a world, built around one thing: the rarest rainforest plants on earth.

Stay a while. leafpeople.app
cta: Welcome to Leaf People — follow @leafpeople.app and we'll take you to the jungle every day.

title: Breathe in
caption:
Breathe in.

Wet earth, crushed leaves, something sweet flowering far overhead. The rainforest floor doesn't smell like anything you keep in a pot — it smells alive.

We can't bottle it. But we can bring you the plants that grow in it. Every single day.

🌿 leafpeople.app

title: Meet the Queen
caption:
Meet the Queen. 👑

Anthurium warocqueanum — three feet of black-green velvet hung from a rainforest tree, one of the most coveted plants on the planet.

Most people will never see one in person. Here, she's only the beginning.

title: What is Leaf People
caption:
So what is Leaf People?

A field guide, a care tracker, an ID engine and a collector's marketplace — built only for rare rainforest plants. Not ten thousand species skimmed. The ones actually worth knowing, studied deep.

By plant people, for plant people. leafpeople.app 🌿
cta: Welcome to Leaf People — follow @leafpeople.app and we'll take you to the jungle every day.

title: Find the light
caption:
Find the light.

On the forest floor it arrives in pieces — a shaft here, a glow there, filtered through a hundred feet of canopy. It's why these leaves grow so big, so dark, so hungry.

Slow down. Let your eyes adjust. There's a whole world down here.

title: Blackest leaf
caption:
The blackest leaf in the room.

Anthurium 'Ace of Spades' drinks the light — velvet so dark it reads almost black, with an oil-slick shimmer when it turns.

Some plants are pretty. This one is a statement.

caption:
Why we built Leaf People.

Because if you've ever fallen down a 1am rabbit hole trying to tell two velvet anthuriums apart, you know the tools out there weren't made for us.

So we made our own. Identify, track, learn, collect — all in one place.

title: Rain on leaves
caption:
The sound of rain on leaves.

Not the city kind — the jungle kind. Fat drops drumming on giant foliage, running down a leaf the size of your arm, feeding roots that never go thirsty.

Close your eyes. You're there.

🌿 #rainforest #leafpeople

title: Silver lightning
caption:
Silver lightning.

Those veins on Anthurium crystallinum aren't painted — it's the way the velvet scatters light. Sugar-white over deep forest green.

Nature engineered this. We just can't stop staring.

title: Deep not wide
caption:
We went deep, not wide.

Anyone can list ten thousand plants. We chose a handful of genera — the rare rainforest aroids and their cousins — and learned them properly. Light, humidity, substrate, the lot.

Quality over quantity. Always.

title: Morning mist
caption:
Morning mist.

For an hour after dawn the cloud forest disappears into white — every leaf beaded with water, the whole world hushed and dripping.

This is the calm we're chasing. A pocket of jungle, two feet from your couch.

🌿 #leafpeople #calm

title: The deep end
caption:
The ones collectors whisper about.

Anthurium papillilaminum — deep, suede-dark, impossibly velvet. The kind of plant that starts bidding wars and long flights to nurseries you've never heard of.

This is the deep end. Welcome.

You're not the only one. 🌿

There's a whole community of people who love these plants like family — who name them, photograph them, mourn a lost leaf.

Leaf People is home base for all of us. Pull up a chair.

caption:
Your own pocket of jungle.

You don't need a greenhouse or a plane ticket. One rare leaf on a shelf, catching the morning light, is enough to take your whole mind somewhere greener.

That's the magic. That's why we're here.

title: The Queen, up close
caption:
She doesn't grow leaves. She grows banners.

Anthurium warocqueanum: two, three feet of black-green velvet catching light like crushed silk. You don't decorate with a plant like this — you keep it.

title: Understory
caption:
This is where they actually live.

Not a windowsill — the understory. Dappled light, dripping humidity, a canopy a hundred feet up. Understand the home, and you understand the plant.

title: Crystalline veins
caption:
Look closer.

The silver veins on Anthurium crystallinum aren't painted on — it's how the velvet scatters light across the surface. Sugar-white lightning over deep green.

title: More than a phone
caption:
Yes, people pay thousands for a single plant.

A rare velvet anthurium can change hands for the price of a used car. Sounds insane — until you see one in person and watch the room go quiet.
cta: Follow @leafpeople.app for the rarest plants on earth, daily.

title: The obsession
caption:
It starts with one leaf.

Then you're three forums deep at 1am learning to tell two species apart by their petioles. Welcome — you're one of us now.
cta: Follow @leafpeople.app for the rarest plants on earth, daily.

title: Ace of Spades
caption:
The blackest leaf in the room.

Anthurium 'Ace of Spades' — velvet so dark it drinks the light, with a faint oil-slick sheen when it turns. Some plants are pretty. This one is intimidating.

title: Green wall
caption:
Imagine your whole wall doing this.

Layered leaves, every shade of green, a private little rainforest two feet from your couch. Not a plant — a feeling. Calm, alive, yours.
cta: Follow @leafpeople.app for the rarest plants on earth, daily.

title: Bone-white veins
caption:
The gold standard of veining.

Thick, heart-shaped, bone-white veins carved into deep green velvet — the leaf people draw when they imagine a 'jungle plant.' Real. Living. Growing on someone's shelf right now.
cta: Follow @leafpeople.app for the rarest plants on earth, daily.

title: Why so rare
caption:
Why is it so hard to get?

Many grow on one mountainside, in one country, and take years to reach a single sellable leaf. Add export rules, slow propagation, and a wall of demand. Scarcity isn't hype here — it's botany.
cta: Follow @leafpeople.app for the rarest plants on earth, daily.

title: First rare plant
caption:
Remember your first 'real' rare plant?

The one you saved for, tracked down, unboxed with your heart in your throat — then checked on six times a day for a week.

Drop it in the comments. 👇
cta: Follow @leafpeople.app for the rarest plants on earth, daily.

title: Velvet up close
caption:
Velvet, but make it alive.

The matte, light-eating surface of a velvet Anthurium comes from tiny cell structures that kill reflection — it feels like suede and photographs like a shadow. No filter.
cta: Follow @leafpeople.app for the rarest plants on earth, daily.

title: Morning dew
caption:
Morning, in the jungle and on your shelf.

Dew beads on a waxy leaf, the light goes soft, and for a second your apartment is a cloud forest. Who else checks their plants before they check their phone?
cta: Follow @leafpeople.app for the rarest plants on earth, daily.

title: Quilted & bullate
caption:
Run your eyes over that surface.

Bullate leaves pucker between the veins — quilted, three-dimensional, catching light in a dozen directions at once. Texture is the whole point.
cta: Follow @leafpeople.app for the rarest plants on earth, daily.

title: Variegation lottery
caption:
The variegation lottery.

Every so often a leaf unfurls half-cream, half-green — a random mutation no grower can guarantee. You can't farm luck. That's exactly why collectors chase it.
cta: Follow @leafpeople.app for the rarest plants on earth, daily.

caption:
